NIFTY NES supply / demand · first BOS builds the zone · sweep + micro-BOS enters it

The whole day is one state machine. 1 — after 09:15 the first candle to CLOSE beyond a confirmed swing (pivot 3) sets the day's direction; a wick through is not a BOS. 2 — the zone is the last opposite-colour candle before that displacement, taken as its full high–low range: a bullish BOS builds demand, a bearish BOS builds supply. 3 — price comes back and touches the zone; the entry is the close of that touching candle — long in demand, short in supply. One trade per day.
Stop — a market order 100 points from the entry, below it for a long and above it for a short, placed with the entry. Risk = 100 points on every trade. Trail — once the trade is 40 points in favour, the stop moves to 30 behind the best price and is re-set each completed 1-minute candle the best price improves; it only ever tightens. A stop that fires after the trail switched on is a TRAIL STOP; before that it is a plain STOP at −100. Exits are market orders, so the fill is the print at the minute the level trades, not the level itself — the slip column shows by how much. Target — the rule has no fixed target: the trailing stop is the exit (the trail tab). The 1:0.5 / 1:1 / 1:2 / 1:3 and liq tabs are shown for comparison and mean “the same trail, but also take profit at that level”. Every fixed target above 100 was measured to make less than the trail, because only 13 of 86 trades ever reach +200 and the rest give back their move waiting. The split-half block below flags any tab whose two halves disagree.
If the zone gives way — a candle closing beyond its far edge by more than the fail buffer — the setup is dead and the day is over. There is no flip and no reversal.
Swings never repaint: a pivot needs 3 candles after it to confirm, so at candle i the newest usable swing is the one at i−3. Signals stop at 15:15; open positions are square off at the session close time. The rule is decided on NIFTY spot, but the money is the option that would actually have been bought: ATM strike at entry, nearest expiry on/after the day, long → CE and short → PE, filled at that contract's 1-minute closes. The ₹ column is premium × 65, not NIFTY points × 65 — the latter is a futures payoff and overstates a bought option. Reward : risk is the real one — average winning premium against average losing premium — and return on premium is net premium over premium deployed. Rows with no option data stay in the table and are left out of the money totals. Shorts are scored as Entry − Exit.
A target reached inside a candle beats that candle's close; when one minute both touches the target and trades the stop, the stop is taken first.
